summary.text: A 49-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder, abstinent for one year before liver transplantation for end-stage alcohol-related liver disease, developed fluctuating global confusion, disorientation and agitation three weeks after the transplant. Vital signs were normal and there was no fever, focal neurological deficit or neck stiffness.

Laboratory testing showed abnormal liver function, hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, with sterile cultures and normal glucose, ammonium and blood alcohol. Electroencephalogram showed mild generalized slowing rhythm and brain MRI showed hyperdensity of the pale nucleus. Wernicke’s encephalopathy was diagnosed from the alcohol history, malnutrition, radiological findings, symptoms and response to thiamine.
He was treated with thiamine 200 mg t.i.d. and haloperidol 5 mg/day and showed improved clinical conditions and remission of neurological symptoms after three days.

summary.text: A 57-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder who had been transplanted for alcohol-related cirrhosis developed delirium about two weeks after liver transplantation. There were no focal neurological deficits, neck stiffness, miosis or mydriasis, and glucose, ammonium, electrolytes, liver and renal function were normal.

Electroencephalogram showed mild generalized slowing rhythm and cranial MRI on T1-weighted image showed contrast enhancement of the medial thalami and around the periventricular region of the third ventricle. Wernicke’s encephalopathy was diagnosed from the alcohol history, malnutrition, radiological findings, symptoms and response to thiamine.
Clinical conditions improved and delirium disappeared after treatment with thiamine 300 mg/day, with complete remission of the altered mental status after four days of thiamine administration.

summary.text: A 51-year-old man with end-stage liver disease related to alcohol abuse and hepatitis B infection developed Clostridium difficile colitis in the days after liver transplantation, treated with metronidazole and oral vancomycin. One week after transplantation he developed confusion, tremor and an altered gait with broad base. Vital signs were normal with no fever or focal neurological deficit.

Liver function was markedly altered, with hypocalcemia and hypomagnesemia, sterile cultures and unremarkable chest X-ray and brain CT. Electroencephalogram showed nonspecific temporal lobe abnormalities and cranial MRI showed a cross-shaped T2 hyperintense signal of the transverse pontine fibers and cerebellar atrophy. Wernicke’s encephalopathy was diagnosed.
He was treated with thiamine 200 mg t.i.d. and haloperidol 5 mg/day and showed an improvement of clinical conditions and remission of neurological symptoms after three days.
